conventions: Where a demonstrative pronoun stands written in the phrase - ha-melakim ha-elleh, ha-yom ha-hu, ha-yom ha-zeh - that pronoun takes the ASV's these, those, this or that, and both the noun's own article and the demonstrative's agreement article are unrepresented. This is rule 41's limit read with a written demonstrative in the place its suffix example occupies: a present morpheme licenses the determiner before the article can. Taken in JOS.10.14, 16, 22, 23, 24, 27, 28, 35 and 42. Name the competing reading in the note: the corpus records four noncompositional ha+hu -> that units, which fuse the agreement article with the demonstrative under rule 30 instead, and that reading is defensible on the one-English-word condition. Two riders this chapter needed. Where the phrase is the rectum of a construct chain and the ASV therefore writes a second determiner - the necks of these kings, JOS.10.24 - the noun's article takes that written the, fronted to the construct under rule 29, and only the agreement article goes unrepresented. And an ordinary attributive that is not a demonstrative is rule 47's plain case rather than this one: ha-yom ha-sheni -> the second day (JOS.10.32) gives the written the to the first article and leaves the agreement article unrepresented.

The conquest refrain le-fi-hereb -> with the edge of the sword (JOS.10.28, 30, 32, 35, 37, 39) is divided the same way in all six: le takes with, the construct pi takes the edge with a supplied the, and hereb takes of the sword with the second supplied the. No article morpheme stands anywhere in the phrase, so neither the is fronted from anything and each noun carries the one written before it; do not give both to the construct or read the second as part of an English compound.

lo hish'ir sarid -> he left none remaining (JOS.10.28, 30, 37, 39, 40): the negative takes none, the noun sarid takes remaining, and the verb keeps he left with its subject pronoun under rule 17. Do not read none remaining as one rendering of sarid. Where the clause is 'ad bilti hish'ir-lo sarid -> until he had left him none remaining (JOS.10.33), 'ad keeps until and bilti takes the none, the ASV having spent a word on each, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is unmet; the dative le is unrepresented under rule 40 and its suffix takes him.

A relative the ASV supplies is placed by what stands in the Hebrew, and this chapter has both cases. For a finite clause merely juxtaposed to a written antecedent - we-ha-seridim sardu -> the remnant which remained (JOS.10.20) - the which is added under rule 55, since rule 46 does not reach such a clause and the article has already taken the phrase's the. Where instead a determined noun is recast verbally - kol ha-neshamah -> all that breathed (JOS.10.40) - every English word must come from the two morphemes present, so the article takes the that under rule 41 and the noun takes breathed.
report: Checked all 76 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket traces to a difference the ASV actually writes and the source licenses: the waw's connectives (Now, Wherefore, So, Then, therefore, but, or, even, also, that), the article's *the* against nothing, the object marker unrepresented against rule 16's *of* (v.19) and *against* (v.25), min as partitive, ablative and comparative, and the ASV's made war/fought, slew/smote, he had done/he did. None is one construction analysed two ways.

The lemma table is blind to `added` units, so I read the dump end to end for supplied English folded in one verse and marked added in another. The three added units - the italic *for* (v.9), *while* (v.11), *which* (v.20) - are each a subordinator standing over a clause with no conjunction and no relative morpheme in it (rule 55), and no other verse folds such a word into a neighbouring morpheme.

Counted each clause's conjunction morphemes against the ASV's connectives, verse by verse. Only JOS.10.20 is out of balance - four waws against three connectives - and s024 is unrepresented, which is the surplus-waw half of rules 14 and 42, not a folded coordinator. No verse carries a surplus English and/but/or absorbed into a preposition, verb or noun.

Audited the article across every construct chain. Where the rectum carries an article and the ASV writes one *the*, it is fronted onto that article (the people of war, the mighty men of valor v.7; the book of Jashar, the midst of heaven v.13; the fortified cities v.20; the men of war, the necks of these kings v.24); where the ASV writes a *the* for each word, the article takes its own and the construct a supplied one (the kings of the Amorites vv.5-6; the mouth of the cave vv.18, 22, 27); where no article morpheme stands, the construct takes the supplied one. The correction recorded in JOS.10.24's review notes agrees with the rest of the chapter rather than departing from it.

Audited the recurring conquest formulae, which are where a split would hide: with the edge of the sword (vv.28, 30, 32, 35, 37, 39), all the souls that were therein (vv.28, 30, 32, 35, 37 twice, 39), he left none remaining (vv.28, 30, 33, 37, 39, 40), as he had done to X (vv.1, 28, 30, 39 twice, 40). Each is analysed identically in every occurrence; the only variations are ones the ASV writes - a written *the* in v.32's the second day against the bare *that day* of vv.28 and 35, an article morpheme present on nephesh in vv.28-37 but absent in v.39, and the bare *that day* of v.35 that leaves its preposition unrepresented under rule 40.

Directive he, presentative frames and demonstratives all hold. Sd takes the ASV's to/unto in vv.6, 15, 31, 34, 36 (Hebron), 38, 43, and is unrepresented in v.36 (Eglon) and v.39 only where min and le have already taken the direction word, which is rule 32's own condition. Rule 45 is applied three ways as the verse requires: apodosis waw takes *that* in vv.11 and 24, the verb keeps it in v.27, and vv.1 and 20 write no *that* at all.

BSB: none of the 49 disagreements is a genuine error. The Td (25), To (12) and R (8) classes are the documented ASV/BSB convention difference over unrendered articles, object markers and recast prepositions; the v.6 paragogic he is rule 32's first sentence; the v.36 and v.39 directive hes are rule 32's last sentence, where another morpheme already carries the direction; the v.20 waw is the surplus counted above. I changed no accepted edge to move the aggregate.

Four chapter-wide judgments are recorded in the conventions log, which had nothing in it against 99 repeated notes. No promotion: the one judgment that generalises - a written demonstrative pronoun licensing the phrase's determiner, so both articles go unrepresented - is contradicted by the corpus, which records 4 noncompositional ha+hu -> *that* units alongside 315 single-token ha -> *that*, so the reading is contested and the convention says so rather than the contract.
